metadata.scenario: A prospect shares their disappointment with the quality of the pest control service, noting that pests are still present. Category: Service Complaint. Flags: quality_complaint.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret speaking. How can I help you today? Hi, Margaret. This is Michael Brown. I found your number from the hospital discharge planning department. Hi, Michael! Thanks for reaching out. What can I assist you with today? Well, my father has diabetes and he needs wound care and medication management, but... I'm actually really disappointed with the quality of service we've been getting from our pest control provider. I'm sorry to hear that, Michael. So, you’re looking for assistance for your father, right? Yes, but the pest issues have been affecting him and it's just frustrating. I understand how important a comfortable home environment is, especially for someone managing diabetes. Can you tell me more about your father's needs? He needs regular wound care for his foot and help managing his medications properly. We can certainly help with that. Our skilled nursing care includes medication management and wound care. That's good to know. How often would he need those services? Typically, we schedule visits based on individual needs. For wound care, it could be 1-2 times a week. Okay, and how much is that? Our skilled nursing care is priced between $95 and $125 per visit for 1-2 hours. That sounds reasonable. Can you also help with his diabetes management? Absolutely! We offer diabetes management services as well, which are around $70 to $85 per session. Great! But back to my concern about the pests... I understand that’s frustrating. While we specialize in healthcare, I recommend contacting pest control directly for that issue. I’ve already done that, but they aren’t addressing the problem effectively. It's just disappointing. That’s truly unfortunate, Michael. Let’s focus on how we can support your father's health needs. Yes, please! I want to ensure he’s well taken care of. I can set up an appointment for an intake assessment. Would you like to discuss a preferred schedule? Yes, how soon can we get someone out for that? We typically have availability within a few days. How does this Friday sound? Friday works for me. What time? Would 10 AM be convenient for you? Yes, that works! Perfect! I’ll schedule your father’s intake for Friday at 10 AM. Thank you, Margaret. I really appreciate your help. You’re welcome, Michael! Is there anything else you need assistance with today? No, that’ll be all for now. Thank you again! It’s my pleasure! Have a great day, Michael. You too. Goodbye! Goodbye!
